summary:
Hello! I am Saqeef Sami, a Class 4 student from India and the solo creator and team leader for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. My project addresses Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.
To tackle this challenge, I researched, wrote, and designed an original narrative project spotlighting the retired spacecraft, rovers, and landing hardware NASA left behind on the lunar and Martian surfaces—including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Mars rovers like Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity, etc. Drawing from official NASA mission archives, engineering logs, and planetary imagery, I distilled complex aerospace history into an accessible, compelling story tailored for school-age audiences.
The project is organized into clear chapters examining why mass constraints required Apollo hardware to remain on the Moon, how entry and landing debris—such as parachutes, heat shields, and skycranes—scattered across Mars, how Opportunity operated nearly fifteen years past her planned ninety-day mission, etc. Through focused storytelling, custom visuals, and concise technical breakdowns, the work explains how these machines functioned and why they remain preserved today.
By bridging authentic aerospace records with thoughtful design, this project honors NASA's silent pioneers on the Moon and Mars and inspires young learners to explore space history.
details:
What Our Project Does & How It Works:
Team Victory Voyage created an original, illustrated true-story book titled Abandoned but Not Forgotten, chronicling the real-life mission of NASA's Mars Opportunity rover etc. Using authentic NASA engineering logs, telemetry data, and Martian surface records, we translated complex scientific history into an engaging, chapter-by-chapter adventure written specifically for school-age space enthusiasts.
Benefits & Intended Impact:
Technical space websites can be difficult for young students to understand. Our storybook bridges that gap by inspiring kids to learn real planetary science, engineering resilience, and the history of human space exploration through an emotional, easy-to-follow true story.
Tools & Creative Process:

To make sure this story wasn't just entertaining, I verified every single mission fact, timeline, and engineering detail directly through NASA's official app and mission archives—so kids are learning 100% authentic space science without even realizing it. At the same time, I knew that regular textbooks and heavy data tables feel boring to young readers. That is why I carefully crafted and designed every page with bold visuals, relatable character storytelling, and bite-sized fun facts that immediately grab a kid's attention and keep them hooked from start to finish. Instead of just reading about abandoned metal on the Moon and Mars, young learners feel the excitement of landing on another planet, exploring alien terrain, and discovering why these silent machines are true space heroes. By blending verified NASA science with playful, kid-first design, this project turns space history into an unforgettable adventure that sparks genuine curiosity in the next generation of explorers.
